chat.content: Welcome to AI-VTT. Drag the highlighted token to move (gold outline = legal range), press End Turn to pass, and describe actions here for the AI Dungeon Master. Campaign: Lost Mine of Phandelver (21 documents loaded).

📖 Previously on…

Previously on our adventure... It began on the morning of the first day, when your old friend Gundren Rockseeker, a dwarf with big plans and a bigger grin, came to you with a job. He needed a wagon loaded with mining supplies hauled to Barthen's Provisions in the frontier town of Phandalin, and he trusted you to see it there safely. For your trouble, Gundren made you a promise: ten gold pieces each, paid in full once those supplies are delivered to Barthen's.

But Gundren would not be making the journey alongside you. He rode on ahead toward Phandalin in the company of Sildar Hallwinter, a seasoned warrior, leaving the wagon, its cargo, and the long road in your hands. Now the reins are yours, the supplies are waiting, and somewhere ahead your friend expects to see you roll into town. The road to Phandalin stretches out before you... so tell me, how do you begin?
[Astarion] did we begin

Yes, we've begun! Here's where things stand. In Neverwinter, your dwarf friend Gundren Rockseeker hired the four of you to haul a wagon of mining supplies to Barthen's Provisions in the frontier town of Phandalin, for ten gold pieces each on delivery. Gundren was excited and secretive, saying only that he and his brothers had found something big, then rode ahead with a warrior named Sildar Hallwinter to take care of business. You've spent a few days following the High Road south, and this morning you turned east onto the Triboar Trail. Two oxen plod ahead of a creaking wagon loaded with flour, salted pork, kegs of ale, picks, shovels and lantern oil. Bandits are known to haunt this road.

Before we roll on, I need two things. First, who is holding the oxen's reins on the wagon? Second, what's your marching order: who rides, who walks alongside, who scouts ahead, and who watches the rear? And a quick reminder: keep your printed location maps covered until you've explored those places. So, Astarion, where do you want to be as the wagon rolls on?
[Astarion] hysterian is on the starboard side of the wagon

Got it. Astarion walks along the right-hand side of the wagon, the starboard side as a sailor would say, one hand resting near the hilt of his shortsword, his pale eyes sweeping the tree line while the dust of the trail settles on his fine boots, much to his visible annoyance. Now I need the rest of the party. Someone has to hold the reins, or the oxen simply stop. Is Edric, Raechyl or Shadowheart driving the wagon? And where are the other two: riding in the back among the flour sacks, walking on the left side, scouting ahead, or watching the rear? Who's holding the reins?
[Astarion] Rachel is holding the reins Patrick is the side or scouting a Ford and Shadow heart is is the side Rachel

Understood. Raechyl takes the reins, Shadowheart sits on the bench beside her, Astarion walks the right side of the wagon, and Edric scouts a little way ahead. The morning passes quietly: birdsong, creaking axles, the oxen's slow plod, and the smell of pine as the woods close in around the Triboar Trail. By midday the hills grow steeper and the trees press tight to the road. Edric is the first to round a bend, and he stops. About fifty feet ahead, two dead horses lie sprawled across the trail, blocking the path. Each bristles with several black-feathered arrows. Here the woods crowd right up to the road, with a steep earth embankment and dense thickets on either side. Flies buzz in the still air. Reminder: if you have the printed map of this roadside, keep it covered for now. The wagon can't get past the horses without moving them. Edric, you're in front: what do you do, and what do the others do?
↳ The party arrives at Roadside trail in the hills (battle map)
🎒 Time: Day 1, 12:00 (midday)

Thanks for telling me! Then forget the printed maps: everything happens right here on the map canvas, and the table only shows you what your characters can actually see, so there's nothing to keep covered. Back on the trail, the wagon creaks to a halt at the bend. Fifty feet ahead, two dead horses lie across the road, black-feathered arrows jutting from their flanks, flies droning in the noon heat. The trees and thick bushes crowd close on both sides beneath steep earthen banks, and the woods have gone strangely quiet. Edric is out in front, Raechyl holds the reins with Shadowheart beside her, and Astarion stands on the right of the wagon. You can walk up to the horses, look them over from where you are, search the bushes, or anything else you think of. Edric, what do you do?

Edric raises a hand to halt the wagon and studies the road ahead, scanning the dirt around the dead horses, the thick bushes at the foot of the banks, and the shadows under the trees. That's a Wisdom check using Perception. Edric, roll a d20 and add 3. The result decides what he notices from where he's standing: tripwires, loose earth, or anything else out of place. If you don't have dice handy, just say 'roll for me' and I'll roll it. What did Edric get?
[Astarion] I rolled a six
🎲 Edric Wisdom (Perception) (player rolled): 6 + 3 = 9

Edric, that's a 9. He squints down the trail, shading his eyes against the noon glare. He sees no tripwire, no freshly turned earth and no rope glinting across the road. Just churned mud, scattered hoofprints and the two dead horses, black-feathered arrows jutting from their sides as flies drone over them. The thick bushes at the foot of the banks are dense, green and still, and from here he can't see more than a few feet into them. As far as Edric can tell, the road itself is clear. To learn more about the horses, whose they are, how long they've been dead and what happened, someone will have to walk up and take a closer look. The wagon waits at the bend, the oxen snorting at the smell of blood. Do you send someone forward to look at the horses, approach all together, or try something else? What does the party do?

Astarion slips forward from the side of the wagon and falls in at Edric's shoulder, light on his feet despite the dust he so clearly resents. From here the two of them look down the trail at the dead horses fifty feet ahead: their saddles still strapped on, black-feathered arrows standing out of their flanks, flies circling lazily. The bushes on either side of the road stay thick and still, and the steep earth banks rise behind them. The road looks quiet. Raechyl and Shadowheart wait on the wagon bench behind you, the oxen shifting uneasily at the smell of death. Do the two of you walk up to the horses for a closer look, call the wagon forward, or try something else? What do Astarion and Edric do?

Up close she recognises them at once: Gundren's sturdy pony-horse and Sildar's tall grey, the same mounts they rode out of Neverwinter. They've been dead about a day, and it was the arrows that killed them, crude black-feathered shafts sunk deep in their flanks.
